meaning: The number of registered men in the tribe of Issachar
description: The number 54,400 is given in Numbers 1:29 as the count of fighting men in the tribe of Issachar, recorded during the first census in the wilderness of Sinai. This census was carried out at the Lord's command shortly after leaving Egypt and included all men twenty years old and older who were able to go to war. The tribe of Issachar remained relatively stable throughout the wilderness journey; by the second census in Numbers 26:25, the tribe numbered 64,300, an increase of nearly 10,000. Issachar was the fifth son of Jacob and Leah, and the tribe later became known for its insight and understanding of the times. In the arrangement around the tabernacle, Issachar was placed on the east side together with Judah and Zebulun, under Judah's banner.

footnotes.text: The name Issachar (יִשָּׂשכָר) is traditionally interpreted as "he brings reward" or "there is a reward," linked to the account in Genesis 30:18 where Leah says, "God has given me my reward."

In 1 Chronicles 12:32, the sons of Issachar are described as men who "understood the times and knew what Israel should do." Rabbinic tradition connects this to knowledge of calendar calculation and astronomy.

The census in Numbers 1 had both military and theological significance: it organized the twelve tribes of Israel as a holy army under God's leadership, where each tribe's number confirmed God's blessing and the fulfillment of His promise to Abraham of numerous descendants.
